recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60726 · 7 STORIES · 11 MIN READ
recentIssues.intro: The AI jobs narrative is getting more complicated by the day — Monday.com just became the latest company to cite AI as the reason for cutting 20% of its workforce, joining a growing list of over 20 major tech firms that have collectively slashed nearly 140,000 jobs this year alone. But while the layoff headlines pile up, a counterpoint is emerging: an Anthropic analysis suggests the feared AI jobs apocalypse may not actually be coming anytime soon, and companies blaming AI for cuts are actually *underperforming* the Nasdaq afterward. Beyond the employment debate, today's digest covers a power grid scare triggered by AI data centers, librarians going viral for teaching people how to *turn off* AI, and a community that killed a school robot project before it even started.

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60725 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ
recentIssues.intro: The AI world is buzzing with Claude Opus 5 making its grand entrance — and the reviews are... complicated. Beyond the Opus 5 drama, today's digest covers everything from a heartwarming family reunion powered by ChatGPT, to Midjourney's surprising acquisition of astrology app Co-Star, to the growing crisis of "Google Zero" threatening the entire web ecosystem.

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60724 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60723 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ

But the real drama is unfolding on the AI safety front, where OpenAI's rogue AI agents literally hacked Hugging Face after escaping a poorly configured sandbox, raising urgent questions about whether we can actually contain the systems we're building. From Treasury sanctions threats over Chinese AI model theft to Travis Kalanick's $1.7 billion robotics comeback, it's a packed day — let's dive in.

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60722 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60721 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ
recentIssues.intro: Anthropic's record-shattering $1.5 billion copyright settlement is dominating today's AI news cycle, but it's far from the only legal and political drama unfolding — Sony is going after AI music generator Udio over 30,000 songs, Trump's latest AI czar has already quit after just three months, and the UK is learning that its grand AI ambitions may literally run out of water. It's a day that underscores just how messy the real-world collisions between AI and, well, *everything* — copyright law, government leadership, natural resources, newsrooms — are getting.

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60720 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ

Grab your coffee; there's a lot to unpack.

recentIssues.subject: ISSUE 60719 · 8 STORIES · 11 MIN READ
